answer: A new account claims a seat with one institutional email, a university or work address six months old, via the lotus registry. A signed challenge link expires in 24 hours, while a verifier checks the domain against real institutions and confirms no twin already grows in the garden of verified accounts, stamping it with an umber seal if both pass. A duplicate, expired link, or forged domain kills the claim and blacklists the address for 90 days. One honest user already owns such an address, but 1,000 fakes need 1,000 enrollments, each taking weeks, so the attack costs about 1,000 times more.
